pill.desc: colorless to pale yellow solution in a prefilled syringe

tell: Made in Escherichia coli and injected into the eye, this VEGF-A binder has a vitreous half-life of about 9 days.

clues.text: Serum concentrations are approximately 90,000-fold lower than vitreous concentrations. No dose adjustment is needed for renal impairment.
Recombinant and humanized, made in an Escherichia coli expression system at about 48 kilodaltons. Supplied as a preservative-free sterile solution.
Approved under a BLA as single-dose prefilled syringes in two strengths, given once a month.
No boxed warning; contraindicated with ocular or periocular infections or hypersensitivity. Conjunctival hemorrhage and eye pain are the most common reactions.
Wet age-related macular degeneration, macular edema after retinal vein occlusion, diabetic macular edema and retinopathy, and myopic choroidal neovascularization.
Binds VEGF-A and blocks its interaction with VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 on endothelial cells, reducing vascular leakage and new vessel formation.
The generic name begins with R and has eleven letters.
